In May, Secretary of State Warren Christopher proposes a 'lift and strike' policy — lifting the arms embargo and using air strikes against VRS positions — but Britain and France reject it. Despite this setback, American diplomatic involvement has begun in earnest. INTELLIGENCE ASSESSMENT ARBiH morale +2 VRS patron pressure +3 American diplomacy enters the Bosnian arena. events.text: 5 5 2 2 2 2 2 DESK WAR MAP ARMY HQ 19 APR 1993 (WAR) RECORDS CHRONICLE CODEX 1 REVIEW Authority is the Presidency resource for exceptional intervention in the command chain. It recovers from political standing and command stability. AUTHORITY 100 REVIEW BLOCKERS ARBIH DECISION REQUIRED Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina · 19 Apr 1993 Srebrenica Demilitarization Agreement PRESIDENTIAL RESPONSE Comply in appearance, hide weapons HISTORICAL DEFAULT This is the historically attested choice. You are free to choose any option. Surrender visible stocks while concealing reserves. The historical choice — preserving minimum defense capability. Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina morale -2 Comply fully with disarmament Surrender all weapons as demanded. Gains international credibility but leaves the enclave with no combat-effective defensive capability under continued VRS pressure. Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina morale -5 Republika Srpska patron pressure +5 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Int'l Standing +10 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Military Credibility -15 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Internal Cohesion -5 Refuse disarmament Publicly reject the agreement. Maintains military capability but repudiates the UN safe-area framework and draws international condemnation and increased VRS pressure. The plan collapses; the war continues but the legal claim to Bosnia's full territory is preserved. events.text: 5 5 2 2 2 3 2 2 2 2 2 DESK WAR MAP ARMY HQ 27 SEP 1993 (WAR) RECORDS CHRONICLE CODEX 1 REVIEW Authority is the Presidency resource for exceptional intervention in the command chain. It recovers from political standing and command stability. AUTHORITY 100 REVIEW BLOCKERS ARBIH DECISION REQUIRED Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina · 27 Sep 1993 Abdic Declares the Autonomous Province PRESIDENTIAL RESPONSE Suppress the breakaway — 5th Corps clearance operations HISTORICAL DEFAULT This is the historically attested choice. You are free to choose any option. Authorize 5th Corps clearance operations against APWB positions in the Velika Kladusa / Cazin sector. Non-recognition holds politically. The operational tempo cascades into Operation Tigar (March 1994), the August 1994 Velika Kladusa clearance, the RS/RSK/APWB Pauk counter-offensive (autumn 1994), and the post-Storm final clearance in August 1995. Costs are paid in 5th Corps personnel and Bihac-pocket supply; the political-recruit posture stays intact. Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina morale -5 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Military Credibility +5 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Internal Cohesion +5 Tolerate the breakaway — concentrate on the external siege Hold 5th Corps to the perimeter against the VRS and RSK and decline to commit forces against APWB. The internal front festers. The SDA hardline current reads the decision as Sarajevo accepting fragmentation; recruitment softens and cohesion erodes as Abdic consolidates Velika Kladusa with VRS and RSK logistical support. The external siege is not relieved. Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina morale -5 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Internal Cohesion -25 Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina Military Credibility -5 Federation-line offer — open dual-track channels Open U.S.-backed Federation-line channels to Abdic with conditional autonomy framings short of formal recognition. The signal is conditional military pressure on the Bihac-pocket axis. Belgrade-aligned Abdic reads the offer as Sarajevo weakness; patron pressure on Sarajevo rises as backers question the discipline of the line, and negotiating leverage drops on the Owen-Stoltenberg / Washington-tra
